title: Trait judgements of faces using a task without word labels
title_zh: 使用无词标签任务对面孔进行特质判断
abstract: Abstract People attribute psychological traits to faces. Previous research has typically elicited these judgements using specific words provided in advance by the experimenter (for example, ratings on competence or trustworthiness), raising questions about completeness (these tasks use a limited set of words) and generalizability (for example, across languages). Here we asked over 3,000 participants to spatially arrange unfamiliar faces based on perceived trait similarity, without providing any word labels. Using predominantly White faces, experiment 1 yielded five dimensions that we interpreted as approachability, gender-specific warmth, competence, morality and youthfulness. Using White, Black and Asian faces, experiment 2 also produced five dimensions, which showed prominent effects of stereotypes associated with race. Comparisons with four other studies that used word labels argue that approachability or warmth emerges as a universal evaluative factor that integrates multiple trait facets (such as trustworthiness, warmth and competence) into a single holistic dimension and that race and gender stereotypes emerge depending on the set of face stimuli used.
abstract_zh: 摘要 人们会将心理特质归因于面孔。以往研究通常通过实验者预先提供的特定词语（例如对能力或可信度的评分）来引出这些判断，这引发了关于完整性（任务使用的词汇有限）和可推广性（例如跨语言）的疑问。本文邀请了3000多名参与者，在不提供任何词标签的情况下，按感知特质相似度对陌生面孔进行空间排列。实验一主要使用白人面孔，得到五个维度，分别解释为亲和力、性别特异性温暖、能力、道德和青春感。实验二使用白人、黑人和亚洲人面孔，也得到五个维度，显示出与种族相关的刻板印象的显著影响。与四项使用词标签的研究比较表明，亲和力或温暖作为一种普遍的评估因素出现，能够将多种特质面（如可信度、温暖和能力）整合为单一的整体维度；而种族和性别刻板印象则取决于所使用的面孔刺激集。
